title: Privnet access mapper: Terraform module for security groups, NACLs, private DNS, and egress policies
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (privnet_access_mapper) that codifies VPC security controls for Private deployments: opinionated security group and NACL templates, automated private DNS (Route53 resolver / conditional forwarders) wiring, and pluggable egress policy enforcement (NAT/Egress Gateway + deny-by-default). The module should be composable for Dedicated and Private stacks, support controlled upgrades, include health checks & monitoring hooks, and emit clear outputs for downstream modules (load balancers, bastions, transit gateways). Aim for idempotent, well-documented variables suitable for customers and internal POCs.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables for allowed service CIDR ranges, admin CIDRs, DNS resolver IPs, and egress-mode (nat|egress-gateway|restricted)
Module provisions Security Groups and NACLs with sane deny-by-default rules and generates an audit report via plan output (changeset summary)
Private DNS: module creates/associates a private hosted zone or configures a managed resolver endpoint depending on cloud, with documented inputs/outputs
Egress enforcement: support for optional egress gateway deployment (sidecar or managed appliance) and automatic routing rules; defaults to NAT where gateway not selected
Health checks: module creates lightweight health checks (route/endpoint monitors) and CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics + alerting hooks (SNS/PagerDuty) and a dashboard link output
Upgrade path documented: clear migration steps when switching egress-mode or changing NACL policies with zero-downtime guidance
Integration tests: unit terraform plan tests and an end-to-end sandbox apply/destroy script that validates connectivity and denies unexpected egress
technical_notes: Implementation details: - Use Terraform module pattern with submodules: sg_templates, nacl_templates, dns_resolver, egress_controller, monitoring_hooks. - Minimal provider assumptions: primary implementation targets AWS (VPC, Security Group, NACL, Route53 Resolver, NAT Gateway, VPC Endpoint routing) but design variables to allow GCP/Azure equivalents later. - Keep state minimal: store IDs and tags; avoid embedding IP addresses as literals. - Use Terraform 1.5+ features (for_each on aws_security_group_rule, count toggles) and lock provider versions. - Implement a 'dry_run' variable that only generates plan output and a human-readable audit summary via terraform local_file (for internal CI). - Health checks: create synthetic endpoint in each AZ (private ALB/target group) and a CloudWatch synthetic check that measures egress path health; provide alerting via SNS topic ARN input. - Upgrade considerations: switching from NAT to EGRESS_GATEWAY requires rolling update of route tables and possible temporary SNAT; provide an automated plan generation script and migration checklist in docs. - Idempotency: prefer aws_network_acl_rule (managed rules) with consistent rule numbers to avoid rule reordering. - Testing: use Terratest for e2e and kitchen-terraform for smoke tests. - Security: module must tag resources and emit IAM policy least-privilege documentation for operator role.

2025-03-11: Spike completed comparing Route53 Resolver vs. conditional forwarders for private DNS; chose Route53 Resolver for AWS-first implementation but added abstraction for other clouds. Notes attached to linked_artifacts.

2025-03-14: Implemented 'egress_mode' variable with three modes (nat, egress-gateway, restricted). Wrote unit tests for SG rules generation. Found an edge case with duplicated NACL rule numbers when using multiple modules; added deterministic numbering scheme.
2025-03-18: Added health-check module prototype and CloudWatch metric filters. Open question for alerts integration with OpsPager on separate ticket (ENG-20322).
review_feedback: PM (Leah Thompson): Ensure defaults are permissive enough for internal POCs but secure for customer templates; prefer explicit 'allow' lists over wide CIDRs.
Security (Ravi Narayanan): Add a toggle to enforce IDS/IPS integration and require KMS key ARN for any private DNS records that contain sensitive metadata.
Design (Sofia Martinez): Document the UX of the 'audit report' output so Console can parse and display policy drift for customers.
Infra (Diego Alvarez): Recommend avoiding reliance on NAT Gateway for high-throughput tenant workloads; call out cost implications and provide telemetry to track NAT egress bytes.
migration_notes: When changing egress_mode from nat to egress-gateway: 1) Provision gateway in parallel, 2) Update route table to point to gateway by AZ with low TTL, 3) Drain NAT connections, 4) Destroy NAT to avoid accidental fallback.
When modifying NACL deny rules: prefer adding explicit deny with higher rule number and monitor for false positives via health-check dashboards before removing old allow entries.
DNS changes: create new private hosted zone and associate VPCs, validate resolver endpoints, then switch records; do not overwrite existing hosted zone names in-place without verification.
notes: Next steps: finish e2e terratest harness, expand cloud-agnostic abstraction layer, schedule security review (requested), and coordinate with Console team to consume audit outputs for policy drift. Owner: Marcus Chen.
